findings: Two-view radiograph of the wrist and distal forearm: posteroanterior (PA) projection on the left and lateral projection on the right
Distal radius demonstrates a transverse fracture with dorsal angulation (apex volar) of the distal fragment visible on the lateral view
On the PA view there is mild radial shortening and loss of normal radial inclination with impaction at the fracture site
The distal ulna styloid process appears intact on the PA view; the distal radioulnar joint relationship appears maintained
Carpal bones appear normally aligned on the PA view; no definite intercalated segment instability pattern identified
No additional metacarpal or phalangeal fractures are identified
Open physes visible at the distal radius and ulna, indicating a skeletally immature individual
No significant soft tissue calcification or foreign body visible
differential: Distal radius fracture with dorsal angulation and impaction (consistent with a Colles-type fracture pattern; given open physes, a Salter-Harris type II physeal fracture cannot be excluded)
Salter-Harris type II fracture of the distal radius physis with dorsal metaphyseal fragment
Torus (buckle) fracture of the distal radius with dorsal cortical buckling (less likely given degree of angulation seen on lateral)
anatomyConcerns: Open physes at both the distal radius and ulna are normal developmental anatomy for a skeletally immature individual and should not be mistaken for fracture lines
The two projections appear to be of the same wrist but are displayed as a composite image; standard orthogonal projections are confirmed (PA and lateral)
Superimposition of carpal bones on the lateral view limits detailed assessment of individual carpal bone alignment
